verdict.line: You lose if you eat a full three-hit Q into a 6-14 all-in, but you win any fight that goes past 3 seconds of extended trading.

brief.thesis: Aatrox wins short trades where he lands his full Q (The Darkin Blade) sweep and follows with Deathbringer Stance; Sett wins everything longer because Pit Grit's empowered auto and W (Haymaker) sustain scale with trade duration while Aatrox has no way to disengage once his cooldowns are down. Play around his Q animation and his E (Umbral Dash) charge count, not his health bar.

theirWindow.when: Q lands all three hits, passive lit
theirWindow.what: He gets a knockup on the edge hits plus a healing empowered auto. Do not extend the trade here — hold W (Haymaker) for the shield and back off until his Q is on cooldown.

yourWindow.when: Q whiffs or he dashes in with E already spent
yourWindow.what: His Darkin Blade cooldown is long when it misses and his Umbral Dash charge is gone until it recharges. Walk him down, land E (Facebreaker) to knock him into a wall for the stun, then all-in with your empowered Pit Grit auto and R (The Show Stopper) if it's up.

powerCurve.note: Maxed Q burst beats your level 1-2 kit
W sustain and E stun offset his poke
R (World Ender) all-in spike is scary
Grit-bar all-ins and armor outscale him

start.why: You want the early sustain and auto damage to punish any Q whiff without falling to his early trade burst.

boots.why: Aatrox's damage is entirely physical auto-attacks and Q hits, so flat armor plus the auto-attack damage reduction directly counters his all-in.

core.why: The auto-attack reset and movement speed burst let you stick through his E dash and land more empowered Pit Grit autos.
Lifedrain procs on crit against a single melee laner give you a sustain edge in every extended trade, which is exactly where you're favored.
The shield and tenacity-adjacent survivability keep you alive through his level 6-8 all-in window until your scaling kicks in.

situational.when: he builds lifesteal or crit and is healing through your trades off Deathbringer Stance
he pairs with magic damage sources or you need to shrug off poke from an aggressive support/jungle
he's snowballed and his empowered autos are one-shotting through your current build
you're ahead and just need insurance against his R all-in reset

runes.keystoneWhy: Sett wins by extending fights, and Conqueror's stacking adaptive damage plus healing is built for exactly the prolonged trades that favor you over Aatrox.

summoners.why: You're favored in skirmishes once trades run long, so Ignite converts your sustain advantage into kills instead of just wins on the wave.

playing.title: Bait the Q before trading
playing.detail: Stand at the edge of his Q range and watch the sweep animation. Sidestep the second and third hits — if you eat all three, you're in his all-in window, not yours.

playing.title: Track the passive icon
playing.detail: Deathbringer Stance ready means his next auto heals him off your missing HP. Never start a trade while it's lit; wait for him to burn it on a minion or bait it out first.

playing.title: Save W for his all-in, not poke
playing.detail: Haymaker's shield and heal are wasted on chip damage. Hold it for the moment he commits with E or Q so it negates his actual burst window.

playing.title: Count his E charges
playing.detail: Before he has 3 souls stacked, Umbral Dash only has one charge on a long cooldown. If he's already used it to engage or reposition, he has zero mobility until it comes back — this is your all-in signal.

playing.title: Respect level 6-8 specifically
playing.detail: World Ender's heal, attack speed, and movement speed make him win fights he'd otherwise lose in this window. Play for freezes and short trades, not all-ins, until you hit level 9.

playing.title: Wall-stun into ultimate
playing.detail: Facebreaker's stun only triggers off collision with terrain. Position trades near river walls or tribrush so a landed E chains directly into The Show Stopper for a guaranteed kill.

playing.title: Don't fight through minion waves
playing.detail: Pit Grit builds off damage taken and dealt in melee range, so soaking wave damage while trading fills your grit bar faster than his passive fills — use big waves to force empowered autos for free.

brief.patchCaveat: Exact numbers for Aatrox's Q cooldown scaling, E charge count thresholds, and Sett's Pit Grit heal ratio may have shifted since my last patch knowledge — verify current tooltips in-client, but the structural read (you win long trades, he wins landed Q into R) has been stable across many patches.
